prompt: Hypothetical. You follow 10 symbols, each at Rs 250. What is the cost of buying one share of each, before charges?
solution: Cost = 10 multiplied by Rs 250 = Rs 2,500, before charges. Check: Rs 2,500 divided by 10 symbols = Rs 250 each.

options.text: It places an order by itself whenever the price is reached, with no setup.
It notifies you when a price level you chose is reached.
It shows the best bid and best ask.

explanations.a: A plain alert only notifies you. Kite's ATO (Alert Triggers Order) can place a basket of orders when an alert fires, but only if you set it up. This book does not rely on an alert to trade.
explanations.c: A stop-loss is part of your written plan. An alert does not set it.
explanations.d: The best bid and best ask are shown in the depth view. An alert does not show them.

prompt: Which description of a watchlist is best?

options.text: A tool for keeping attention on symbols that you have written rules for
A list of stocks the book recommends
A list that places trades automatically

explanations.a: A watchlist does not say that you should buy anything. It only holds your attention.
explanations.c: This book does not recommend stocks, and a watchlist is not a recommendation list.
explanations.d: A watchlist does not place trades. Orders are a separate step that you take with your own plan.

prompt: Hypothetical. A student adds the stock that rose most today to the watchlist and sets an alert at its high. What is the best reply?

options.text: Good. Rising stocks are the best ones to watch.
Check your written rules first. A rise today is not a reason to act, and the alert is only a review prompt.
Good, because the alert will place the order when the price rises.
Wrong. Only falling stocks belong on a watchlist.

explanations.a: A stock that rose most today may not match your rules. Rising is not a reason on its own.
explanations.c: An alert places an order only if ATO was set up for it. Even then, the plan comes first. A rise today is not a reason on its own.
explanations.d: A watchlist can hold any symbol that meets your written rules. Falling is not a rule.

prompt: Spot the mistake. A student writes: 'The alert fired at Rs 252, so I placed an order straight away without checking my plan.' Which part is the mistake?

options.text: So I placed an order straight away without checking my plan.
I set the alert earlier in the day.

explanations.a: This is a fact about the alert. An alert is a notification, so its firing is not the mistake.
explanations.c: Setting an alert earlier is a normal step. The mistake is what the student did after it fired.
